gaps.sentence: She ___ to pass one more exam to qualify as an architect.
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' conjugates like a normal verb: she needs to pass.

gaps.sentence: You ___ not be so hard on yourself — everyone makes mistakes.
gaps.explanation: 'Should not' gives gentle advice against something: should not be.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have told me earlier — I could have helped.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have told' — reproach about the past.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.

gaps.sentence: There ___ be a supervisor present when students use the lab.
He ___ be at work — I've just seen him at the beach.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses something the evidence rules out.

gaps.sentence: He ___ not understand the lecture at all yesterday.
gaps.hint: an inability that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Could not' expresses past inability: could not understand.

gaps.sentence: You ___ touch that wire — it carries a live current!
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' signals something absolutely not allowed: mustn't touch.
